title: Hackers Steal Active Directory Password Hashes Without Attacking Domain Controllers Directly
content_md: Threat actors are increasingly exploiting Active Directory replication mechanisms to steal password hashes without directly compromising a domain controller. This technique, known as DCSync, allows attackers with privileged domain credentials to impersonate a legitimate domain controller and request sensitive directory replication data.
